newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products -- Midco gasoline diffs rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products -- Midco gasoline diffs rally.

text.p: Gasoline differentials shot higher in the Midcontinent Thursday, helped by modest pipeline inventories and refinery problems in Illinois.
However, Gulf Coast and New York Harbor markets were thinly traded as players pulled back to watch the expiration of the August futures on the NYMEX.

August gasoline futures opened firmer but soon fell more than 5 cents, paring much of rally made over the previous few days. The contract expired at 70.30 cents, down 2.06 cents on the day, while August heating oil left the board at 55.61 cents a gallon, down 0.17 cent.
MIDCONTINENT
Group Three unleaded gasoline differentials skyrocketed for very prompt August barrels in line with sharp gains in Chicago earlier Thursday and amid expectations for a drop in inventories.

Players said they were expecting a huge decline in inventories along the Williams Pipeline system because the high value of U.S. Gulf conventional unleaded made it too expensive to ship up from Houston into the Midwest.
The Williams system is fed by the Houston-to-New York Colonial Pipeline network.
"About 800,000 barrels of gasoline that was nominated to go from the Gulf to us is no longer coming," said a Midwest gasoline trader.
In late Thursday trade, very prompt Group Three unleaded sold for 7.15 cents over the September NYMEX futures, up 3.50 cents since this morning. Any months were up by a quarter at 2.50/2.75 cents.

Chicago held in its lofty range of 6.00/7.00 cents a gallon, bid up by heavy buying late Wednesday and Thursday morning by Mobil Oil. There was talk the company's cat cracker at its 203,700 barrel-per-day Joliet, Illinois, refinery had problems.
U.S. GULF
Conventional M1 gasoline differentials eased modestly by late day, though traders said few interested players were seen in the market.
"It was extremely quiet today. Everybody's cleaning up their books," one Gulf player said. "We don't expect anything tomorrow either."

Prompt M1 gasoline was quoted between 0.50 and 0.75 cent over the September futures, a drop of about 0.40 cent from Wednesday's levels, while any-month barrels were seen steady at 3.00 cents under the September.
Prompt reformulated A1 gasoline was seen at a 3.00-cent premium to the M1, or about 3.50 cents over the September NYMEX, according to traders.
Gulf heating oil prices were talked slightly firmer, with offers sitting near 2.35 cents under the September futures.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Lackluster trading also characterized the Harbor Thursday, with many traders awaiting the expiration of the August futures.
Prompt conventional M2 gasoline was seen near 2.50 cents under the August NYMEX, though few takers were evident given the sharp swings in the outright price, according to market watchers.
Reformulated A2 gasoline remained firm, with prompt barrels seen hovering between 3.25 and 3.50 cents over the August futures, traders said.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
